title: Vantage / Answer and share a cost question
goal: Narrow spending, inspect its composition, compare it and share the same analysis.
route: Filter → group → drill into a parent → inspect children → compare → export
scope: 6 official documentation screenshots. Different example reports and dates; this is a documented workflow map, not a continuous session recording.
adopt: One analysis scope should survive every drill-down and the exported report.
avoid: Changing only the table when a user groups the chart.
gap: A saved-report confirmation is described in documentation but not captured here.

steps.title: 01 / Define the scope
steps.description: Choose provider, dimension and matching rule. The filter is visible before analysis begins.
steps.next: Next: choose how to break down that scope.

steps.title: 02 / Reveal composition
steps.description: Group selections change the segmented time chart; its colors distinguish cost contributors.
steps.next: Next: investigate a business grouping.

steps.title: 03 / Pick a parent group
steps.description: The table exposes nested business units and a drill-down control beside each row.
steps.next: Next: expand the relevant unit.

steps.title: 04 / Inspect its children
steps.description: Application-level rows appear under the selected unit, retaining the parent context.
steps.next: Next: compare the costs that matter.

steps.title: 05 / Compare periods
steps.description: Paired bars make current and previous costs directly comparable for each category.
steps.next: Next: share the analysis.

steps.title: 06 / Share an evidence snapshot
steps.description: The exported document retains report identity, dates, costs, series and a link back.
steps.next: Outcome: a reviewable report rather than an isolated number.

title: DoiT / Investigate and resolve an anomaly
goal: Determine whether a spike is meaningful, inspect contributors and record the response.
route: Observe deviation → find contributors → investigate scope → classify → explain → preserve history
scope: 7 official help-center screenshots. Examples span different workloads, providers and dates; do not interpret their amounts as one reconciled incident.
adopt: Carry anomaly scope into analysis, and preserve classification, explanation and actor history.
avoid: Showing a spike without expected values or treating every increase as waste.
gap: No authenticated incident was changed; saved-state behavior was not exercised.

steps.title: 01 / Establish the deviation
steps.description: Excess cost, actual cost, expected ceiling and event timing precede a chart with the normal range.
steps.next: Next: inspect the contributing resources.

steps.title: 02 / Identify contributors
steps.description: Rows expose SKU, account, resource, tags and monetary contribution for investigation.
steps.next: Next: open the scoped report.

steps.title: 03 / Explore the event context
steps.description: The report combines a segmented chart with provider, service and billing filters.
steps.next: Next: decide how to classify the incident.

steps.title: 04 / Classify the response
steps.description: Investigation progress is separate from whether the detected increase is genuine or expected.
steps.next: Next: record the resolution context.

steps.title: 05 / Explain the resolution
steps.description: A classification form offers structured reasons and a place for context before saving.
steps.next: Next: make the reasoning available to others.

steps.title: 06 / Preserve discussion
steps.description: Dated comments retain the investigation narrative alongside the resolution.
steps.next: Next: inspect the recorded event history.

steps.title: 07 / Verify traceability
steps.description: The timeline exposes status transitions, actors and notification activity.
steps.next: Outcome: later reviewers can reconstruct the response.

title: CloudZero / Turn an investigation into tracked work
goal: Connect a spending change to resources and capture the finding for follow-through.
route: Business view → change contributors → resource evidence → create Insight → track → return to context
scope: 6 official documentation screenshots, published as separate examples. Values and selected resources differ between screens; the navigation relationship is documented.
adopt: A finding should carry its evidence link, impact and work status into the team queue.
avoid: Separating the recommendation story from the analysis that supports it.
gap: The creation form and resulting queue are examples, not a replay proving one item was saved.

steps.title: 01 / Orient around business ownership
steps.description: A business-unit chart pairs total cost with a comparable change, showing composition over time.
steps.next: Next: inspect the largest contributors.

steps.title: 02 / Rank changes, not only spend
steps.description: Resource rows pair total cost with absolute and percentage change; decreases remain visible.
steps.next: Next: inspect a resource.

steps.title: 03 / Check the resource context
steps.description: A drawer combines resource trend, configuration summary and cost-allocation tags.
steps.next: Next: capture a finding in the investigation context.

steps.title: 04 / Record a finding
steps.description: The form captures title, category, description, impact, an analysis link, status and effort.
steps.next: Next: track it with other findings.

steps.title: 05 / Manage the work queue
steps.description: An impact summary and status distribution sit above a searchable, filterable findings table.
steps.next: Next: reopen a finding.

steps.title: 06 / Resume with context
steps.description: The detail panel retains description, impact and an Explorer return path beside its work controls.
steps.next: Outcome: the finding remains connected to the original investigation.

title: nOps / Prioritize, evaluate and implement savings
goal: Find worthwhile opportunities, assess consequences and follow implementation progress.
route: Opportunity feed → prioritized summary → recommendation evidence → instructions → savings history
scope: 5 vendor-published screenshots from a November 2025 announcement. This is a public example workflow, not a tested account; no AWS action was executed.
adopt: Effort, implementation constraints and evidence belong beside the savings estimate.
avoid: Copying an execution shortcut into CloudLens, which does not change AWS infrastructure.
gap: A completion confirmation is not shown. The source calculates savings tracking from recommendation estimates; independent causal measurement is unproven here.

steps.title: 01 / Surface opportunities in context
steps.description: The feed brings recommendation themes into a recurring work surface.
steps.next: Next: review the opportunity portfolio.

steps.title: 02 / Prioritize by return and effort
steps.description: The page separates potential savings, effort bands and achieved savings above actionable themes.
steps.next: Next: inspect one recommendation.

steps.title: 03 / Evaluate impact and constraints
steps.description: The detail example shows estimated saving, effort, age, current/projected cost and implementation considerations.
steps.next: Next: review the procedure.

steps.title: 04 / Understand implementation
steps.description: A separate instruction view explains the resource-specific procedure and cautions.
steps.next: Next: implementation happens outside this research exercise.

steps.title: 05 / Review the savings history
steps.description: The history distinguishes accumulated savings from a recurring monthly savings rate.
steps.next: Outcome shown: historical savings reporting; measurement methodology must be checked.

title: Datadog / Move from recommendation to owned action
goal: Filter opportunities, inspect operational evidence and hand off implementation.
route: Overview → filtered queue → resource evidence → tracked handoff | alternative: native action | upstream: rule tuning
scope: 6 vendor-published screenshots from an August 2025 walkthrough. Cards 04–06 illustrate alternative routes, not mandatory consecutive steps. Datasets differ.
adopt: Pair resource evidence with accountable work and a return link; show changes and impact together.
avoid: Assuming approval, resource execution and verified savings are the same state.
gap: Ticket/case creation entry points are visible; completed ticket histories and achieved savings are not captured.

steps.title: 01 / Find the opportunity mix
steps.description: A summary groups recommendations by savings potential and action category.
steps.next: Next: narrow the queue.

steps.title: 02 / Filter actionable resources
steps.description: Provider and recommendation filters narrow rows containing savings, resource context and status.
steps.next: Next: inspect evidence before choosing an action.

steps.title: 03 / Inspect evidence and ownership route
steps.description: The resource panel compares current/proposed configuration with CPU or memory evidence and a case entry point.
steps.next: Next: create owned work or choose another route.

steps.title: 04A / Hand off to a tracked issue
steps.description: Selected resources can be grouped into an implementation ticket from the queue.
steps.next: Branch outcome: a linked work item, not proof of implementation.

steps.title: 04B / Alternative: scoped execution
steps.description: An action form exposes connection, region, volume and approval/notification controls.
steps.next: Alternative route only; execution was not tested.

steps.title: Upstream / Tune recommendation rules
steps.description: Evaluation window, resource scope and rationale can be configured for the organization.
steps.next: Feedback loop: adapt detection to operational constraints.

title: AWS / Configure monitoring, then investigate
goal: Separate monitored scope from delivery rules, then connect an alert to investigation.
route: A: monitor list → define scope → subscription list → alert rules   /   B: anomaly investigation → explanation
scope: 6 official screenshots. A uses a historical March 2023 walkthrough. B uses a June 2026 investigation release. These are explicitly separate versions and sequences.
adopt: Keep monitoring scope, notification policy and incident evidence distinct.
avoid: Treating older AWS screenshots as a current visual specification, or assuming detection is immediate.
gap: No save confirmation or alert delivery was exercised. Current permissions and availability require account-level validation.

steps.title: A1 / Review monitored scopes
steps.description: The historical monitor table names each scope and its monitor type.
steps.next: 2023 example → create or adjust a monitor.

steps.title: A2 / Define what to monitor
steps.description: The setup form separates monitor type, linked accounts and naming.
steps.next: 2023 example → configure notification delivery.

steps.title: A3 / Review subscriptions
steps.description: A separate list exposes thresholds, frequency, subscribers and attached monitors.
steps.next: 2023 example → edit delivery conditions.

steps.title: A4 / Set delivery conditions
steps.description: Recipients, schedule and combined dollar/percentage conditions are explicit inputs.
steps.next: Documented endpoint: save the subscription; confirmation not pictured.

steps.title: B1 / Start an evidence investigation
steps.description: The newer anomaly interface offers an Amazon Q investigation entry point.
steps.next: Separate 2026 sequence → inspect the resulting analysis.

steps.title: B2 / Inspect the analysis
steps.description: The published explanation illustrates contextual investigation rather than a standalone total.
steps.next: 2026 example; no live query or causal claim was tested here.

title: CloudHealth / Partner reporting references
goal: Understand the distinct commercial questions answered by customer reports.
route: Parallel report destinations: invoice reconciliation | customer cost history | partner margin history
scope: PARTIAL COVERAGE • 3 official report screenshots with historical 2017–2018 example data. These are parallel reports, not a captured end-to-end customer onboarding flow.
adopt: Keep partner commercial data separate from customer-facing consumption context.
avoid: Adding invoices or reseller margin to CloudLens: those are outside the PRD scope.
gap: Current tenant selection, report configuration and delivery screens were not available in this reference set. Do not claim a complete live MSP flow.

steps.title: Reference A / Reconcile invoices
steps.description: The report identifies customer, invoice month and billed total for reconciliation.
steps.next: Separate commercial task, not an engineering investigation.

steps.title: Reference B / Compare customer spending
steps.description: A monthly stacked chart separates customer contributions to partner-managed spending.
steps.next: Use to understand cross-customer consumption changes.

steps.title: Reference C / Review partner economics
steps.description: The margin chart answers a reseller profitability question rather than a client usage question.
steps.next: Keep this outside the proposed CloudLens homepage.

title: Flexera One / Lifecycle evidence and screen gap
goal: Understand documented state transitions without inventing missing product screens.
route: Documented route: savings summary → recommendation table → detail/action menu → snooze or reject
scope: PARTIAL COVERAGE • One official state diagram, not a product screenshot. The linked documentation describes UI steps; this pass did not obtain a complete public screenshot sequence.
adopt: Status definitions must explain timing and the effect on potential savings.
avoid: Drawing plausible interface screens and presenting them as competitor evidence.
gap: Missing: summary, table, detail, action dialog and success screens. Documentation says marking Realized is API-only; do not invent a matching UI button.

steps.title: Vendor diagram / State relationships
steps.description: The diagram distinguishes active, deferred, rejected and realized states. It documents relationships, not the interaction design.
steps.next: Read the official status instructions. A product walkthrough is still required for visual validation.
